cycle_time.insight: The gap between median (7.3d) and P85 (23.2d) shows a long right tail: most items finish in about a week, but a meaningful minority take 3x longer, hurting predictability. The improving trend (-0.41 d/wk) is genuine but modest. Bugs show the widest spread (median 5.7d vs mean 17.8d), suggesting a few very slow bugs dominate.
cycle_time.watch_out: Whether the improving trend holds once the recent high-completion weeks normalise.

lead_time.insight: Median lead time (12.0d) is close to median cycle time (7.3d), but the mean (38.6d) and max (624.9d) reveal that many items wait a very long time before or between commitments. The worsening trend (+1.41 d/wk) contrasts with improving cycle time — delay is accumulating upstream, not in delivery.
lead_time.watch_out: Old backlog items being pulled in will keep inflating lead time even if delivery stays fast.

throughput.insight: Average throughput of 6.6/wk with an improving trend (+0.43/wk) is a healthy base for probabilistic forecasting, but the zero-completion week (1 June) followed by 8 completions suggests batchy finishing rather than steady flow.
throughput.watch_out: Whether the strong July/August run reflects genuine improvement or a push to clear aged items.

time_in_columns.insight: Refinement is the dominant bottleneck at 2.39x the average dwell (mean 319h ≈ 13 days), more than double In Progress. This is likely an upstream capacity/prioritisation problem rather than a delivery problem — items sit being 'refined' far longer than they take to build.
time_in_columns.watch_out: Whether Refinement time is active discussion or passive queuing — the median (100h) vs mean (319h) gap suggests a long tail of parked items.

flow_efficiency.insight: Mean flow efficiency of 23% with a median of 0% means most items spend the majority of their life waiting, and half spend essentially no measured active time at all. 245 of 355 items sit below 20%, indicating waiting is the norm, not the exception.
flow_efficiency.watch_out: Median 0% may partly be a measurement artefact (items skipping active columns) — verify column mapping before acting.

work_start_efficiency.insight: The median wait before development is only 0.3 days — most items start promptly once committed. But the mean of 17.4 days shows a subset of items languish long after commitment, likely the same aged items inflating lead time.
work_start_efficiency.watch_out: Items committed early to 'reserve' them but not actually started.

wip.insight: Current WIP of 24 with 10 items in Refinement confirms inventory is concentrated upstream. Delivery-stage WIP (In Progress 6, In Test 0-1) is modest, so the multitasking risk sits in refinement and ready queues rather than in development.
wip.watch_out: The 5 items in Ready — a queue between two queues, adding pure wait time.

wip_over_time.insight: WIP drifted upward from ~24 to peaks of 38-39 mid-window (+0.55/wk trend) before falling back to 25 recently. The trend suggests WIP is accumulating passively rather than being actively capped, though the recent drawdown is encouraging.
wip_over_time.watch_out: Whether the recent drop is deliberate WIP management or just a completion burst.

wip_age_distribution.insight: 14 of 24 in-progress items are over 30 days old, with a mean age of 62.7 days and P85 of 127.8 days. The dominant over-30-day band indicates the team routinely starts work it does not finish promptly, undermining any cycle-time forecast for new starts.
wip_age_distribution.watch_out: Aged items eventually completing will spike reported cycle times despite the improving trend.

wip_age_by_column.insight: Ageing is concentrated upstream: Ready holds items at a median of 127.8 days and Refinement has items up to 259.9 days old, while In Progress median is a healthy 9.7 days. This is systemic parking in pre-development stages, not a delivery-stage ageing problem — except two Ready-for-Release items at 205.9 days that appear forgotten near the finish line.
wip_age_by_column.watch_out: The three ~128-day Ready items (1198320-22) appear to be a batch parked together — likely a stalled initiative.

blockers.insight: Blocking is rare but devastating when it happens: ever-blocked items show a 637.7% median cycle-time uplift (50.9d vs 6.9d) and spend 36.2% of their cycle under a blocker. This suggests the team lacks an effective escalation path once something is blocked, so blocked items are set aside rather than actively unblocked.
blockers.watch_out: Item 497159 blocked 945.9 days in Backlog — likely a zombie item skewing blocked-days totals.

blocked_by_signal.insight: Blocking is dominated by generic 'Blocked' (6 items) with only 1 'Waiting on Microsoft', so the signal taxonomy tells us little about impediment causes. Coarse labelling makes it hard to distinguish internal dependencies from external vendor waits.
blocked_by_signal.watch_out: Consider richer blocker categories (dependency, decision, environment) to make this data actionable.

blockers_by_column.insight: The single currently blocked item sits in Backlog, meaning active delivery is currently unimpeded. Blocking here is a demand-side/backlog hygiene issue right now, not a delivery-side one.
blockers_by_column.watch_out: Historical blocked items completed slowly, so watch new blocks in delivery columns closely.

blocker_timeline.insight: Blocked counts have been stable at 1-2 per week for the whole window with a brief spike to 4 in early August. Blocking is a persistent low-level condition rather than an escalating trend.
blocker_timeline.watch_out: The August spike to 4 — check whether those items were resolved or absorbed silently.

days_lost_to_blockers.insight: 90 total days lost is entirely attributable to one long-running block, and the sole current blocked item has been blocked for 945.9 days — far exceeding any plausible active time. Blocking here is structural abandonment, not incidental delay.
days_lost_to_blockers.watch_out: Decide-or-delete policy needed for items blocked longer than a quarter.

stale_work.insight: 220 items untouched for 30+ days — the vast majority backlog items in 'New' state with a suspicious cluster at exactly 35.8 days (likely a bulk update event). This volume of dormant work makes the backlog unreliable as a planning instrument and hides genuinely valuable items.
evidence: cluster at exactly 35.8 days since update
stale_work.watch_out: The 35.8-day uniformity suggests a bulk edit reset timestamps — actual staleness may be far worse.

net_flow.insight: Departures (7.5/wk) now exceed arrivals (6.5/wk) into the delivery workflow, and the last four weeks are all positive net flow — the team is draining its in-progress inventory. This is sustainable and healthy at the workflow level, though it contrasts with system-wide accumulation seen in the CFD.
net_flow.watch_out: Positive net flow driven by a slowdown in starts (3-5/wk recently) — throughput will fall if intake stays low.

arrival_departure.insight: All workflow columns show balanced arrival/departure ratios (0.94-1.06), meaning no column is structurally accumulating within the board. The bottleneck expresses itself as dwell time in Refinement, not as unbounded queue growth.
arrival_departure.watch_out: Balance can mask slow flow — items move through at matched but slow rates.

bugs.insight: 36 open bugs with 28 sitting untriaged in Backlog, while bug completions are batchy (0 most weeks, 6 in one week). Bugs are ~21% of WIP, a moderate quality tax, and resolution appears to happen in cleanup pushes rather than continuously.
evidence: 6 bug completions week of 2026-08-03 vs 0 most weeks
bugs.watch_out: Untriaged Backlog bugs — unknown severity risk lurking in 28 items.

bug_intake.insight: Bug creation runs at roughly 2-3/wk with a recent uptick (5 in early August), while completions total 16 vs ~30 created in-window — the team is accumulating quality debt at a slow but steady rate.
evidence: ~30 bugs created vs 16 completed in window
creation spike of 5 (2026-08-03) and 3+2 in following weeks
bug_intake.watch_out: The August creation spike coincides with the high-throughput delivery weeks — possible quality trade-off.

bug_pct.insight: Bugs make up 20.8% of WIP but only 17% of completions (15/86), so bugs are being carried slightly disproportionately to their resolution rate. Not alarming, but a fifth of active capacity going to defects reduces feature delivery.
bug_pct.watch_out: If bug WIP share climbs above ~25%, feature velocity will visibly suffer.

bug_net_flow.insight: Cumulatively the team created more bugs than it closed this window, with resolution concentrated in late July/early August. Persistent slightly-negative bug net flow means quality debt is growing gradually and will require a deliberate paydown.
evidence: 9 of 14 creation weeks had zero completions
bug_net_flow.watch_out: Weeks where creation and delivery both spike (2026-08-03: 5 created, 14 items delivered).

bug_distribution.insight: 28 of 36 open bugs sit in Backlog untriaged, with only 2 in active delivery columns. The risk is not delivery-stage congestion but invisible severity — untriaged bugs can't be prioritised against features.
bug_distribution.watch_out: The 3 null-column bugs need column assignment or closure.

cfd.insight: System-wide arrivals (11.2/wk) exceed departures (9.7/wk) with a 'growing' accumulation signal, driven almost entirely by Backlog (avg 134.9 items) and Refinement (88.6). The CFD confirms the time-in-columns bottleneck: work piles up before development, while delivery bands stay thin (2-11 items).
evidence: avg Backlog 134.9 and Refinement 88.6 vs In Progress 10.6
cfd.watch_out: Refinement averaging 88.6 items vs 10 on the board snapshot suggests a large hidden refinement queue — verify board vs data scoping.

wip_level_distribution.insight: Refinement has no WIP limit and is never empty (modal 10, reaching 22), confirming it as the uncontrolled constraint. In Progress exceeds its limit of 10 on 19.8% of days and Ready for Release exceeds its limit 23.1% of days, while In Test is empty 19.8% of the time — limits exist but are not enforced, and test capacity is intermittently starved.
evidence: Refinement: limit 0, never empty, up to 22 items
In Progress over limit 19.8% of days
Ready for Release over limit 23.1% of days; In Test empty 19.8%
wip_level_distribution.watch_out: Ready for Release regularly holding 6-10 items suggests batched or infrequent releases.

diagnostic_findings.finding: The primary constraint is upstream: work waits in Refinement/Ready far longer than it takes to build.
evidence: Ready column median WIP age 127.8 days
In Progress median item age 9.7d and median cycle time 7.3d
CFD: Backlog+Refinement average ~224 items vs ~19 in delivery columns
diagnostic_findings.interpretation: Delivery capacity is adequate; the system starves on decision-making and readiness of work, inflating lead time while cycle time stays healthy.
plausible_explanations: Items entering refinement before they are genuinely wanted
No entry criteria or WIP limit on Refinement
Stakeholder decisions pending on parked items
diagnostic_findings.what_would_confirm_this: Review the 10 items currently in Refinement with the PO: how many have an active decision pending vs are simply parked?

diagnostic_findings.finding: Cycle time improving while lead time worsens indicates delay is shifting upstream, not being eliminated.
evidence: median wait before dev 0.3d but mean 17.4d
diagnostic_findings.interpretation: Once work truly starts it flows well; the growing lead time is old committed items ageing in queues before development.
plausible_explanations: Old backlog commitments being pulled in late
Commitment made too early relative to capacity
Batch planning creating long ready queues
diagnostic_findings.what_would_confirm_this: Decompose lead time into pre-start vs post-start components for the last 20 completions.

diagnostic_findings.finding: Recent healthy net flow is partly driven by reduced starts, not just increased finishing.
evidence: starts fell from 14 (wk 2026-07-20) to 3-5/wk in the last three weeks
diagnostic_findings.interpretation: The team is draining inventory, which is good, but throughput will drop if intake stays low — the July completion peak reflects clearing accumulated WIP.
diagnostic_findings.what_would_confirm_this: Ask the team whether reduced starts were deliberate; watch throughput over the next 3 weeks.

diagnostic_findings.finding: By Little's Law, current WIP is consistent with observed cycle time, but total system WIP is not.
evidence: workflow WIP ~31 avg / throughput 6.6/wk ≈ 4.7 weeks, matching P85 CT of 23.2d
system-wide Refinement avg 88.6 items ≈ 13+ weeks of supply
diagnostic_findings.interpretation: The delivery board is roughly right-sized, but the refinement pipeline holds a quarter-plus of inventory, guaranteeing long lead times for anything entering now.
plausible_explanations: Backlog used as a wishlist rather than a commitment queue
diagnostic_findings.what_would_confirm_this: Count refinement-stage items with a realistic delivery slot in the next two quarters.

diagnostic_findings.finding: Blocking is rare but catastrophic — a systemic escalation gap rather than frequent impediments.
evidence: 637.7% median CT uplift for blocked items
diagnostic_findings.interpretation: Blocked items are shelved rather than escalated, so a single block predictably turns a 7-day item into a 50-day item.
plausible_explanations: No blocker SLA or escalation path
Blockers on external parties with no leverage
diagnostic_findings.what_would_confirm_this: Walk the history of the 6 ever-blocked items: who owned unblocking, and how long between block and first escalation?

diagnostic_findings.finding: Ageing work is tolerated, especially in 'ready' queues, and quality debt is slowly compounding alongside it.
evidence: bugs created (~30) exceed bugs closed (16) in window
diagnostic_findings.interpretation: The system lacks age-triggered review; items pass refinement then stall, and defect debt grows quietly beneath the improving delivery numbers.
diagnostic_findings.what_would_confirm_this: Standup review of every item >30 days old with an explicit finish/park/kill decision.

outlier_patterns.pattern: A trio of PBIs parked in Ready at identical ages — a likely stalled batch/initiative.
evidence: recent column moves (0.7-6.7 days in current column) despite old age
outlier_patterns.possible_meaning: A feature set was refined together ~4 months ago and never scheduled; recent shuffling suggests indecision rather than progress.
outlier_patterns.recommended_follow_up: Ask the PO whether this initiative is still wanted; if not, remove from Ready.

outlier_patterns.pattern: Extremely old items still 'in flight' upstream and at the release gate.
evidence: 1156052: 205.9d old, sitting in Ready for Release
outlier_patterns.possible_meaning: Zombie items that inflate WIP age and will distort cycle-time stats if ever completed; 1156052 is finished work delivering no value.
outlier_patterns.recommended_follow_up: Release or close 1156052 immediately; make explicit keep/kill decisions on the Refinement zombies.

outlier_patterns.pattern: One item blocked for over 2.5 years.
evidence: accounts for the dominant share of blocked-time history

outlier_patterns.recommended_follow_up: Check whether release cadence or sprint-end rituals gate completions.

outlier_patterns.pattern: Bulk-updated stale backlog masking true item ages.
items_or_periods_involved: ~180 items at exactly 35.8 days since update
evidence: identical days_since_last_update values across most stale items
outlier_patterns.possible_meaning: A bulk edit reset update timestamps ~5 weeks ago; genuine staleness is likely much greater and the backlog is largely dormant.
outlier_patterns.recommended_follow_up: Sample 20 of these items with the PO to estimate what fraction are still wanted; consider a backlog purge policy.

executive_summary.headline: The team delivers quickly once work truly starts, but a large, ageing queue of undecided work upstream is making overall delivery promises slower and less reliable.
executive_summary.narrative: When this team picks something up, it usually finishes within about a week, and their finishing rate has been rising. The problem sits before that point: a large pile of requests waits months for decisions about whether and when to do them, and that waiting period is getting longer. Several pieces of work have been sitting part-finished or parked for four to eight months, including one finished item waiting at the release gate for no clear reason. A handful of items that hit obstacles took seven times longer than normal, because obstacles tend to be set aside rather than actively cleared. Meanwhile, slightly more defects are being reported than fixed, so quality debt is slowly building. The fix is not working harder — it is deciding faster, trimming the waiting pile, and putting a spotlight on anything that has stalled.
executive_summary.primary_diagnosis: An unmanaged upstream queue (refinement and ready stages) with no limits or age policies is the system's main constraint, inflating lead time despite healthy delivery-stage flow.
executive_summary.main_caveat: Timestamp anomalies (a bulk update ~5 weeks ago and a 0% median flow efficiency) mean some waiting-time measurements may be under- or mis-stated; the direction of the diagnosis is solid but exact magnitudes are not.

recommendations.action: Introduce a WIP limit and maximum-age policy on Refinement.
recommendations.why: Refinement is the measured bottleneck (2.39x average dwell, no limit, never empty, items up to 260 days old).
recommendations.first_step: Set a limit of 6 and review every Refinement item older than 30 days for keep/kill this week.
recommendations.metric_to_watch: time_in_columns (Refinement mean hours) and lead time trend
recommendations.expected_effect: Lead time trend reverses within 6-8 weeks as parked items are decided or removed.

recommendations.action: Run an ageing-WIP review in every standup for items older than 14 days.
recommendations.why: 14 of 24 in-flight items exceed 30 days; ageing is currently invisible to daily conversation.
recommendations.first_step: Sort the board by item age tomorrow and make an explicit decision on the top five oldest.
recommendations.expected_effect: Over-30-day WIP halves within a month.

recommendations.action: Establish a blocker escalation SLA (e.g. escalate any block older than 3 days).
recommendations.why: Blocked items suffer a 638% cycle-time uplift, indicating blocks are shelved not solved.
recommendations.first_step: Assign a named unblocking owner to every raised blocker; close the 946-day zombie block on item 497159.
recommendations.metric_to_watch: blockers ct_impact uplift and longest block duration
recommendations.expected_effect: Blocked-item cycle times converge toward 2x rather than 7x normal.

recommendations.action: Release item 1156052 and investigate the Ready-for-Release queue cadence.
recommendations.why: Ready for Release exceeds its WIP limit 23% of days and holds a 206-day-old finished item — value is being delayed after the hard work is done.
recommendations.first_step: Ship or close 1156052 this week and map the release approval steps.
recommendations.metric_to_watch: wip_level_distribution for Ready for Release; time in that column
recommendations.expected_effect: Faster value delivery and reduced release-column dwell.

recommendations.action: Triage all 28 Backlog bugs and reserve a small continuous bug-fix capacity.
recommendations.why: Bug creation (~30) exceeded resolution (16) this window and fixes currently happen in batches.
recommendations.first_step: One-hour triage session; tag severity on all open bugs.
recommendations.metric_to_watch: bug net flow (weekly creations vs completions)
recommendations.expected_effect: Bug net flow reaches balance within 4-6 weeks.

recommendations.action: Purge or archive the dormant backlog (220+ stale items).
recommendations.why: A backlog dominated by untouched items obscures priorities and inflates lead-time statistics when old items are pulled.
recommendations.first_step: Auto-flag anything untouched 90+ days for PO confirmation; archive non-responses after two weeks.
recommendations.metric_to_watch: stale_work count and lead time mean/median gap
recommendations.expected_effect: Backlog shrinks to a plannable size; lead time mean converges toward the median.

recommendations.action: Formalise the recent 'finish before start' behaviour as an explicit pull policy.
recommendations.why: The last four weeks of positive net flow and falling WIP coincided with the best cycle times — make it deliberate, not accidental.
recommendations.first_step: Agree a total workflow WIP cap (e.g. 25) at the next retro.
recommendations.metric_to_watch: wip_over_time trend and cycle time P85
recommendations.expected_effect: P85 cycle time falls below ~18 days and stays there.

data_quality_caveats: A large cluster of items shows exactly 35.8 days since last update, indicating a bulk edit that reset timestamps — true staleness is likely understated.
Median flow efficiency of 0% suggests many items may skip or not register time in 'active' columns; the active/waiting column classification should be validated.
One item blocked 945.9 days dominates blocker totals and inflates days-lost figures.
3 open bugs have a null current column, indicating incomplete board mapping.
The 3-month window includes only 6 ever-blocked completed items, so blocker impact statistics rest on a very small sample.
CFD arrival rate (11.2/wk, includes Backlog intake) differs from workflow arrival rate (6.5/wk) by design; they measure different workflow stages.
Ready column shows some items with old total age but very recent column entry (0.7 days), suggesting recent board restructuring or re-mapping that may affect column-dwell accuracy.
